hero_palestrina_sistine_choirbook.name: hero_palestrina_sistine_choirbook
hero_palestrina_sistine_choirbook.description: Monumental Late-Renaissance Sistine Chapel choirbook hand (c. 1585): upright broad-nib lozenge noteheads, center-piercing stems, all-vocal pennant flags, and heavy walnut iron-gall ink.
hero_palestrina_sistine_choirbook.paleography_notes: Models late-16th-century Cappella Sistina giant folio choirbooks (Palestrina circle, c. 1580-1595): wide chisel-cut goose quill (49 deg, 0.16 min-ratio) forming ceremonial upright broad-nib lozenge noteheads (scale 1.34, aspect 1.18) with center-piercing mensural stems, un-beamed vocal pennant flags (all_flags_vocal), archaic double-bar C-clefs, hooked serif barlines, open double-loop rests, and deep walnut iron-gall pooling and bleed-through on thick hand-ruled Roman rag.

hero_monteverdi_vespers_quill.name: hero_monteverdi_vespers_quill
hero_monteverdi_vespers_quill.description: Early-Baroque Mantuan/Venetian dramatic manuscript (c. 1610): rust-amber oxidized iron-gall ink, transitional slim-diamond heads, arched convex beams, and acid-feathered bleed-through.
hero_monteverdi_vespers_quill.paleography_notes: Evokes Claudio Monteverdi's 1610 Mantuan and Venetian theatrical-sacred manuscripts (L'Orfeo / Vespro della Beata Vergine era): corrosive rust-amber iron-gall ink with pronounced acid feathering (0.56) and ghost bleed-through (0.24), transitional slim-diamond noteheads (aspect 0.46), tapered quill stems, sweeping Baroque-curl flags, arched convex beams with mixed vocal/instrumental split grouping, calligraphic broad-nib clefs, pointed teardrop flats, bowed freehand barlines, and wavy hand-drawn rastrum staves.

hero_couperin_versailles_clavecin.name: hero_couperin_versailles_clavecin
hero_couperin_versailles_clavecin.description: Versailles royal clavecin manuscript (Couperin circle, c. 1717): gossamer crow-quill pinprick noteheads, tall spindly stems, French broken secondary beams, and filigree scrolled clefs.
hero_couperin_versailles_clavecin.paleography_notes: Models Parisian and Versailles court clavecin manuscripts (François Couperin / Philidor atelier, c. 1713-1730): razor-pared crow-quill producing gossamer hairlines (stroke_scale 0.54) and miniature pinprick-dot noteheads (scale 0.56, aspect 0.50) to leave airy room for agréments, tall spindly stems (1.38x), closed-loop flourish flags, French broken secondary beaming with hairline-thin beams, lavish baroque ornate scroll clefs (clef_ornate 0.99), hairline needle accidentals, crisp vertical barlines, and delicate needle-S rests on luminous ivory laid paper.

hero_anna_magdalena_bach_notebook.name: hero_anna_magdalena_bach_notebook
hero_anna_magdalena_bach_notebook.description: Anna Magdalena Bach's 1725 Leipzig domestic keyboard notebook: warm chestnut-sepia goose quill, plump teardrop heads, sweeping concave phrase-long beams, and rhythmic ink-dip cadence.
hero_anna_magdalena_bach_notebook.paleography_notes: Models Anna Magdalena Bach's celebrated Leipzig fair-copy hand (1725 Clavier-Büchlein and Cello Suites copy): warm chestnut-sepia iron-gall ink with visible 22-stroke quill-dip shading, supple goose quill (39 deg, 0.19 min-ratio) forming plump teardrop noteheads (scale 1.06, aspect 1.12) and flared-base stems, signature Bach-circle sagged concave phrase-long beams (sagged_concave / concave_valley / long_phrase_beam), feathered-sweep flags, Baroque vertical flats, figure-8 treble clefs, tapered quill barlines, wide sweeping ledgers, and authentic reversed-r quarter rests on mellow cream Leipzig paper.

hero_vivaldi_turin_concerto_rush.name: hero_vivaldi_turin_concerto_rush
hero_vivaldi_turin_concerto_rush.description: Antonio Vivaldi's presto Venetian concerto working score (Turin collection, c. 1728): wind-swept 17.8-deg slant, boomerang-hook shorthand heads, overhanging swooping beams, and dry split-nib skips.
hero_vivaldi_turin_concerto_rush.paleography_notes: Models Antonio Vivaldi's famously rapid Ospedale della Pietà concerto autographs in the Turin Foà/Giordano collection (c. 1725-1735): flexible quill driven at presto speed with frequent 16-stroke ink dips, heavy split-nib tracks (0.44) and dry-brush dropout (0.34), maximal 17.8-deg forward wind-swept slant, slashing boomerang-hook noteheads (-46 deg, aspect 0.42), whip-taper stems, hurried slash flags, overhanging swooping feathered-splay beams, hurried single-loop clefs, X-shaped sharps, steeply slanted overshooting barlines (0.82 sp), minimal V-tick quarter rests, and severe end-of-bar cramming on warm Venetian rag.

hero_mendelssohn_leipzig_fair_copy.name: hero_mendelssohn_leipzig_fair_copy
hero_mendelssohn_leipzig_fair_copy.description: Felix Mendelssohn's famed Leipzig Gewandhaus fair copy (1835-1847): jeweler-like calligraphic poise in warm chestnut-black iron-gall ink on fine cream manuscript paper.
hero_mendelssohn_leipzig_fair_copy.paleography_notes: Modeled on Mendelssohn's legendary fair copies of the Violin Concerto Op. 64 and Elijah (Leipzig, 1844-1846): impeccably balanced slim-oval noteheads, refined italic quill contrast, gently sloped ribbon beams, immaculate vertical barlines, and serene margin planning with almost zero crowding.

hero_clara_schumann_concert_part.name: hero_clara_schumann_concert_part
hero_clara_schumann_concert_part.description: Clara Schumann's concert performance part (1840-1870): bold, commanding steel-nib legibility with sweeping arched phrase beams, wide-swept ledgers, and poised virtuoso spacing.
hero_clara_schumann_concert_part.paleography_notes: Draws on Clara Schumann's working concert manuscripts and piano parts (Piano Trio Op. 17, Romances Op. 21-22): dark high-contrast steel-nib ink meant to read cleanly by gaslight at the keyboard, generous full-bodied oval noteheads, arched convex long-phrase beaming, flared stem bases, and confident hooked barline serifs.

hero_fanny_hensel_berlin_salon.name: hero_fanny_hensel_berlin_salon
hero_fanny_hensel_berlin_salon.description: Fanny Hensel's Berlin Sonntagsmusiken salon album leaf (1830-1847): luminous, feather-fine plum-sepia ink, gossamer hairline beams, delicate teardrop heads, and poetic cursive grace.
hero_fanny_hensel_berlin_salon.paleography_notes: Inspired by Fanny Hensel's illustrated fair copy of Das Jahr (1841) and Berlin salon Lieder albums: whisper-thin pointed steel-nib hairlines in refined dark plum-sepia ink, slender teardrop noteheads with elongated needle stems, airy high-floating paired beams, faint hairline barlines, and ornate spiral treble clefs on bright cream-white album stock.

hero_rossini_naples_opera_rush.name: hero_rossini_naples_opera_rush
hero_rossini_naples_opera_rush.description: Gioachino Rossini's breakneck Naples/Rome bel canto opera autograph (1815-1823): exuberant 17.5-degree forward cursive velocity, boomerang-hook heads, vocal flags, and rapid burnt-umber quill dips on sun-warmed Italian rag.
hero_rossini_naples_opera_rush.paleography_notes: Modeled on Rossini's famously rapid Italian opera autographs (Il barbiere di Siviglia, Otello, La Cenerentola, 1815-1817): heavy forward-leaning cursive velocity on coarse oblong Venetian/Neapolitan rag paper, boomerang-hook noteheads with whip-tapered stems, vocal all-flag beaming with dramatic swooping overhangs, rapid 16-glyph iron-gall ink dip cycles, and hand-rastrumed curving staves.

hero_berlioz_paris_grand_score.name: hero_berlioz_paris_grand_score
hero_berlioz_paris_grand_score.description: Hector Berlioz's monumental Paris Conservatoire orchestral full score (1830-1860): towering overshooting barlines, dramatic chevron-wedge noteheads, steep French broken-secondary beams, and bold charcoal-iron-gall authority.
hero_berlioz_paris_grand_score.paleography_notes: Modeled on Berlioz's full orchestral autographs (Symphonie fantastique, Harold en Italie, Les Troyens): huge pre-ruled Parisian papier regle folios with abundant blank orchestral staves, heavy dark iron-gall chevron-wedge noteheads, steep jagged tapered-wedge beams using French broken-secondary grouping, tall spindly G-clefs, dramatic overshooting system barlines, and copious instrumentation annotations.

hero_lili_boulanger_prix_de_rome.name: hero_lili_boulanger_prix_de_rome
hero_lili_boulanger_prix_de_rome.description: Lili Boulanger Prix de Rome & Villa Medici autograph (1913-1918) in luminous plum-violet Parisian fountain ink with soaring spindly stems, arched French broken beams, and delicate fragile poise.
hero_lili_boulanger_prix_de_rome.paleography_notes: Modeled on Lili Boulanger's 1913-1918 autographs (Faust et Helene, Psaume 130, Pie Jesu): warm plum-sepia French violet fountain ink on luminous cream Conservatoire paper, slender oval noteheads on soaring tall stems, convex-arched beams with French broken secondary beaming, graceful bowed barlines, airy floating tilde rests, and subtle late-illness hairline tremor.

hero_ravel_watchmaker_micro_nib.name: hero_ravel_watchmaker_micro_nib
hero_ravel_watchmaker_micro_nib.description: Maurice Ravel's legendary Swiss-watchmaker fair copy (1905-1920) drawn with an ultra-fine crow-quill nib in jet-black India ink on crisp white vellum, featuring microscopic pinprick noteheads and hairline beams.
hero_ravel_watchmaker_micro_nib.paleography_notes: Inspired by Maurice Ravel's jewel-like autographs of Gaspard de la nuit, Daphnis et Chloe, and Le Tombeau de Couperin: jet-black ink from a razor-fine crow-quill nib, microscopic pinprick noteheads, needle-thin stems and beams, near-zero motor wobble, crisp vertical barlines, and virtually no erasures.

hero_scriabin_ecstatic_pencil.name: hero_scriabin_ecstatic_pencil
hero_scriabin_ecstatic_pencil.description: Alexander Scriabin's late mystical piano-sonata graphite draft (1908-1915) in soft silvery-charcoal pencil with an ecstatic 17-degree forward slant, flying needle slashes, feathered-splay beams, and smoky eraser clouds.
hero_scriabin_ecstatic_pencil.paleography_notes: Modeled on Scriabin's feverish soft-graphite drafts of the late piano sonatas (Op. 68 Black Mass, Vers la flamme, Prometheus): powdery charcoal pencil texture with heavy eraser smudges, ecstatic 17-degree forward slant, needle-slash noteheads, whip-tapered soaring stems, upward-drifting accidentals, and feathered-splay swooping beams.

hero_mussorgsky_pictures_iron_gall.name: hero_mussorgsky_pictures_iron_gall
hero_mussorgsky_pictures_iron_gall.description: Modest Mussorgsky's St. Petersburg iron-gall autograph (Pictures at an Exhibition, 1874) with broad-nib lozenge noteheads, dramatic dip-pen pooling and feathering, heavy ribbon beams, and tea-stained Russian rag paper.
hero_mussorgsky_pictures_iron_gall.paleography_notes: Modeled on Mussorgsky's 1874 St. Petersburg autograph of Pictures at an Exhibition and Boris Godunov: broad dip-pen saturated in dark oxidized umber iron-gall ink (frequent 16-glyph dip cycles, rich pooling, split-nib grit, strong bleed-through), monumental lozenge noteheads, flared-base stems, serif-hooked barlines, and asymmetric 3+1 Promenade beam groupings.

hero_mahler_vienna_blue_crayon.name: hero_mahler_vienna_blue_crayon
hero_mahler_vienna_blue_crayon.description: Gustav Mahler's Vienna Court Opera & Maiernigg orchestral score revision (1899-1910) slashed in electric cobalt-blue conductor's crayon over dark pre-ruled staves with towering barlines and abundant blank orchestral systems.
hero_mahler_vienna_blue_crayon.paleography_notes: Modeled on Gustav Mahler's iconic Vienna Hofoper and Maiernigg symphonic working scores (Symphonies Nos. 5-9): urgent, waxy Prussian/cobalt-blue conductor's pencil slashing across spacious pre-ruled orchestral paper, bold chevron-wedge noteheads, overhanging long-phrase beams, towering overshot barlines, violent zigzag rests, and dense margin dynamic/bowing directives.

hero_stravinsky_morges_fine_pen.name: hero_stravinsky_morges_fine_pen
hero_stravinsky_morges_fine_pen.description: Architectural 1910s Swiss-period modernist fair copy in obsidian India ink on translucent ivory vellum with razor-thin needle-slash noteheads and asymmetric Stravigor beams.
hero_stravinsky_morges_fine_pen.paleography_notes: Modeled on Igor Stravinsky's Morges and Paris fair copies (L'Histoire du soldat, Les Noces, Symphonies of Wind Instruments, 1914-1920) drafted with his 5-wheel Stravigor roller-rastrum and a fine crow-quill/fountain nib in jet-black India ink on crisp translucent vellum. Signature visual cues: ruler-straight staves, surgical needle_slash heads, hairline_needle stems, angular sharp_angular_7 flags, overhanging_ends beams in uneven_3_plus_1 modernist groupings, sharp_angular_modern clefs, and razor-crisp geometric Z rests.

hero_messiaen_birdsong_cahier.name: hero_messiaen_birdsong_cahier
hero_messiaen_birdsong_cahier.description: Dense mid-century birdsong field notebook in deep aubergine-plum fountain ink with micro vertical-tick heads, feathered splay beams, and profuse species marginalia.
hero_messiaen_birdsong_cahier.paleography_notes: Modeled on Olivier Messiaen's Cahiers de notations des chants d'oiseaux (1941-1960, Bibliotheque nationale de France). Penned outdoors in deep plum-black fountain ink on warm aged rag sheets, packing irrational avian melismas into tiny vertical_tick noteheads, tall_spindly stems, feathered_sweep flags, tight_crammed_bars in feathered_splay groupings with exaggerated_swoop contours, delicate French spiral clefs, crammed_tight_cluster chromatic accidentals, and dense margin annotations logging bird species, hour, and color-chord harmonies.

hero_crumb_makrokosmos_fineliner.name: hero_crumb_makrokosmos_fineliner
hero_crumb_makrokosmos_fineliner.description: Museum-grade 1970s avant-garde graphic calligraphy in 0.2mm Rapidograph black on snow-white Bristol board with luminous diamond heads and floating hairline beams.
hero_crumb_makrokosmos_fineliner.paleography_notes: Modeled on George Crumb's celebrated pen-and-ink masterworks (Makrokosmos Vols. I-II, Black Angels, Ancient Voices of Children, 1970-1979) executed directly for facsimile publication with a tubular Rapidograph technical pen on bright white heavyweight Bristol board. Defined by uniform monoline ink track (nib_min_ratio 0.96, ink_dip_period 0), near-zero wobble, luminous slim_diamond noteheads, center_piercing stems, wide_horizontal_wing flags, hairline_thin beams floating in long_phrase_beam spans, tall_spindly_g clefs, hooked_top_bottom_serif barlines, and sparse pinprick_minimal_v rests.

hero_john_williams_hollywood_pencil.name: hero_john_williams_hollywood_pencil
hero_john_williams_hollywood_pencil.description: Iconic Hollywood film-scoring short-score sketch in powdery 2B graphite on pale cyan Ozalid studio vellum with large legible ovals, eraser ghosts, and studio-clean rests.
hero_john_williams_hollywood_pencil.paleography_notes: Modeled on John Williams's celebrated 12-stave piano-conductor sketches (Jaws, Star Wars, E.T., Schindler's List, 1975-2023) written at the piano in soft 2B/3B graphite on pale cyan-tinted Hollywood Ozalid/reprographic manuscript paper for orchestrators to read at a glance. Characterized by velvety graphite grain, heavy eraser_smudge_prob from rapid cue revisions, generous legible oval noteheads, double_stroke_sketch stems, tapered_wedge beams with engraver_gentle slopes and standard_beat clarity, studio_copyist_clean_3 rests, and abundant orchestral cue/timing marginalia.

hero_morricone_cinecitta_ink.name: hero_morricone_cinecitta_ink
hero_morricone_cinecitta_ink.description: Sweeping Italian film-scoring autograph in rich Roman espresso-sepia calligraphic ink on warm Ricordi buff paper with arched beams and dramatic forward slant.
hero_morricone_cinecitta_ink.paleography_notes: Modeled on Ennio Morricone's self-orchestrated full-score autographs written directly in ink without piano sketch (The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, Once Upon a Time in the West, The Mission, 1964-2000). Trained in Goffredo Petrassi's Roman conservatory tradition, Morricone's hand fuses bold Italian broad-nib calligraphy (nib_min_ratio 0.20, ink_dip_period 22) in deep espresso-sepia ink on warm cream-buff Italian manuscript stock: steep 15.5-degree forward slant, boomerang_hook noteheads, expressive s_curve_flex stems, long_dramatic_s flags, bold arched_convex beams in convex_arch contour, calligraphic_broad_nib clefs, tall_overshoot barlines, and sweeping S-hook rests.

hero_monk_angular_lead_sheet.name: hero_monk_angular_lead_sheet
hero_monk_angular_lead_sheet.description: Angular 1950s Thelonious Monk bebop/modernist lead sheet in bold black chisel-pen ink with chevron-wedge noteheads, counter-sloped beams, stubby stems, and geometric Z-rests.
hero_monk_angular_lead_sheet.paleography_notes: Inspired by Thelonious Monk's 1950s New York copyright lead sheets and Five Spot bandstand charts (e.g., 'Brilliant Corners', 'Straight, No Chaser'). Drawn with a firm broad chisel pen in jet-black ink on warm cream manuscript paper: blunt chevron-wedge noteheads, short stubby stems with a slight idiosyncratic back-lean, contrarian reverse-quirk beam slopes grouped in snappy swung pairs, razor-angular modern clefs, jagged zigzag accidentals, and geometric Z quarter rests.

hero_bill_evans_jazz_pencil.name: hero_bill_evans_jazz_pencil
hero_bill_evans_jazz_pencil.description: Introspective 1960s Bill Evans modal-jazz piano voicing sketch in soft 2B silver-charcoal graphite with airy slim-oval heads, hairline phrase beams, and pervasive eraser smudges.
hero_bill_evans_jazz_pencil.paleography_notes: Evokes Bill Evans's late-1950s and early-1960s harmonic voicing notebooks and trio ballad sketches (e.g., 'Peace Piece', 'Waltz for Debby'). Written with a soft 2B wooden graphite pencil on bright white-ivory manuscript stock: high paper-tooth grain, delicate slim-oval noteheads, gently bowed stems, sweeping long-phrase hairline beams, wispy Chopin-like spiral clefs, floating tilde quarter rests, hollow sketch bar rests, and abundant rub-out clouds from subtle inner-voice reharmonizations.

hero_piazzolla_buenos_aires_tango.name: hero_piazzolla_buenos_aires_tango
hero_piazzolla_buenos_aires_tango.description: Passionate 1960s Astor Piazzolla Buenos Aires nuevo tango bandoneón/quintet autograph in wet midnight blue-black fountain ink with slashing needle noteheads and asymmetric tango beaming.
hero_piazzolla_buenos_aires_tango.paleography_notes: Modeled on Astor Piazzolla's 1960s Buenos Aires Quinteto Nuevo Tango manuscripts (e.g., 'Adiós Nonino', 'Libertango' era) drafted rapidly in wet midnight blue-black fountain-pen ink on warm aged South American rag manuscript stock. Hallmarks include a fierce 15.5 deg forward kinetic slant, razor-thin needle-slash noteheads, steep forward-leaning stems, dramatic exaggerated-swoop tapered-wedge beams in asymmetric 3+1 milonga/tango groupings, calligraphic broad-nib clefs, sweeping S-hook rests, and periodic wet-nib ink surges.

hero_bluenote_van_gelder_ozalid.name: hero_bluenote_van_gelder_ozalid
hero_bluenote_van_gelder_ozalid.description: 1964 Englewood Cliffs Blue Note hard-bop session chart reproduced on pale cyan-blue Ozalid diazo stock with oversized broad-nib lozenge heads, flat studio beams, and chisel lightning rests.
hero_bluenote_van_gelder_ozalid.paleography_notes: Rooted in 1960s New York / Englewood Cliffs hard-bop recording sessions (Blue Note Records at Rudy Van Gelder's studio; Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, and Oliver Nelson horn parts) duplicated on pale blue diazo Ozalid blueprint paper. Engineered for instant sight-reading under dim studio lamps: oversized dark broad-nib lozenge noteheads, heavy upright stems, ruler-flat thick horizontal beams, bold Real-Book clefs and marker accidentals, crisp engraved bar rests, and razor-straight pre-printed staves.

hero_songwriter_spiral_gelpen.name: hero_songwriter_spiral_gelpen
hero_songwriter_spiral_gelpen.description: Everyday contemporary songwriter's late-night spiral notebook in vivid cobalt-blue gel pen with unclosed open-loop noteheads, detached stems, vocal split-flags, and severe end-of-bar cramming.
hero_songwriter_spiral_gelpen.paleography_notes: Captures everyday 21st-century indie/folk/pop songwriting and conservatory melody-jotting in a wire-bound spiral manuscript notebook using a uniform-tip 0.7mm cobalt-blue rollerball gel pen. Immediately distinguished by vivid blue ink on crisp white spiral stock, hastily drawn open-loop noteheads with detached-gap stems, vocal-style mixed split-flagging and overhanging beams, hand-curved staves, awkward backwards-E quarter rests, coffee-cup ring stains, and heavy right-edge measure cramming.

hero_hildegard_bingen_parchment.name: hero_hildegard_bingen_parchment
hero_hildegard_bingen_parchment.description: 12th-century Rhineland Benedictine chant codex (Hildegard von Bingen, Rupertsberg c. 1180): vermilion-red rubricated staves, Gothic Hufnagel chevron-wedge noteheads, short virga stems, and soaring vocal melismas on golden vellum.
hero_hildegard_bingen_parchment.paleography_notes: Models the Rupertsberg Riesencodex and Dendermonde Codex (Hildegard von Bingen circle, c. 1175-1190): luminous cinnabar/vermilion rubricated staff lines paired with dense carbon-black/iron-gall ink on toothy golden calfskin vellum; broad chisel-cut scriptorium quill (52 deg, 0.16 min-ratio) forming Gothic horseshoe-nail (Hufnagel) chevron-wedge noteheads, short stubby virga stems (0.74x), stubby wedge flags (all_flags_vocal), archaic bracket C-clefs, vertical B-rotundum flats, inside-staff divisio breath barlines, and minimal V-tick pauses with a 16-stroke quill-dip cadence.

hero_josquin_cambrai_choirbook.name: hero_josquin_cambrai_choirbook
hero_josquin_cambrai_choirbook.description: Franco-Flemish High Renaissance choirbook (Josquin / Alamire atelier, c. 1505): crisp white-mensural hollow-diamond noteheads, flared calligraphic stems, ribbon vocal flags, and warm bistre-sepia ink on Flemish cream vellum.
hero_josquin_cambrai_choirbook.paleography_notes: Evokes the courtly Franco-Flemish Habsburg-Burgundian and Cambrai Cathedral choirbooks (Josquin des Prez / Petrus Alamire scriptorium, c. 1495-1515): supple broad goose quill (46 deg, 0.17 min-ratio) in warm bistre-sepia ink over lighter umber-ochre hand-ruled staves; classic white-mensural void hollow-diamond noteheads (scale 1.28, hollow_open_prob 0.72), tall flared-base stems (1.18x), flowing calligraphic-ribbon vocal flags (all_flags_vocal), ornate calligraphic broad-nib clefs, open-loop b-molle flats, tapered quill barlines, reversed-r quarter rests, and hollow-box longa/breve rests on luminous cream Flemish paper.

hero_byrd_elizabethan_partbook.name: hero_byrd_elizabethan_partbook
hero_byrd_elizabethan_partbook.description: Elizabethan Tudor royal partbook & virginal fair copy (William Byrd / John Baldwin, c. 1591): open-loop Tudor noteheads, left-bowed stems, double-looped flags, overhanging paired beams, and cool oak-gall ink.
hero_byrd_elizabethan_partbook.paleography_notes: Models John Baldwin's celebrated 1591 fair-copy hand for William Byrd (My Ladye Nevells Booke and Tudor Chapel Royal partbooks): poised, slightly back-leaning English secretary ductus (-2.0 deg) in cool oak-gall umber-slate ink (26-stroke dip period) on fine cream laid paper; open-loop noteheads (aspect 0.78, hollow_open_prob 0.42), subtly left-bowed stems (1.14x), ornate Elizabethan double-back-loop flags, signature Tudor overhanging-end paired beams (pair_beams_2, tight_hug_beam), figure-8 scrolled clefs, pointed teardrop flats, hooked-serif barlines, wide sweeping ledgers, and open double-loop quarter rests.

hero_victoria_avila_cathedral.name: hero_victoria_avila_cathedral
hero_victoria_avila_cathedral.description: Spanish Golden Age cathedral facistol choirbook (Tomás Luis de Victoria, Ávila/Madrid c. 1595): monumental obsidian-black heavy-wedge heads, thick upright stems, flat Iberian flags, and deep iron-gall pooling on toasted ochre rag.
hero_victoria_avila_cathedral.paleography_notes: Models monumental Castilian cathedral lectern choirbooks (libros de facistol of Ávila, Toledo, and Descalzas Reales, Tomás Luis de Victoria era, c. 1585-1605): stark, high-contrast obsidian-black iron-gall ink with frequent 14-stroke broad-reed dipping, heavy pooling (0.60), and acid bleed-through (0.24) on deeply toasted ochre Spanish rag; massive upright heavy-wedge noteheads (scale 1.38, fill_density 1.38), heavy-thick vertical stems, stark rectangular flat-bar vocal flags (all_flags_vocal), double-bar C-clefs, oversized bold accidentals, wide-double-gap cathedral barlines, bold chevron rests, and thick smudged bar rests.

hero_gesualdo_ferrara_madrigal.name: hero_gesualdo_ferrara_madrigal
hero_gesualdo_ferrara_madrigal.description: Late-Renaissance Mannerist chromatic madrigal score (Carlo Gesualdo, Ferrara/Venosa c. 1605): corroded blood-sepia iron-gall, spiky boomerang-hook heads, crammed chromatic accidentals, whip-taper stems, and downward-drifting staves.
hero_gesualdo_ferrara_madrigal.paleography_notes: Evokes the feverish, hyper-chromatic Late-Renaissance Mannerist working scores of Carlo Gesualdo, Prince of Venosa (Ferrara court & Gesualdo Castle, c. 1594-1611): dark oxidized blood-sepia iron-gall ink with corrosive acid feathering (0.48), split-nib scratches (0.32), and 17-stroke dip surges; steeply slanted (15.5 deg) spiky boomerang-hook noteheads, agitated whip-taper stems (1.26x), long dramatic S-flags, stepped wobbly beams with exaggerated swoop slopes (mixed_split_flags), hurried single-loop clefs, notoriously crammed-tight chromatic accidental clusters, freehand S-wobble barlines, sweeping S-hook rests, knife-scraped smudges, and melancholic downward-sloping staves (-1.35 deg) on shadowed antique rag.

hero_scarlatti_madrid_sonata.name: hero_scarlatti_madrid_sonata
hero_scarlatti_madrid_sonata.description: Domenico Scarlatti's Madrid royal court harpsichord sonata copy (c. 1752): razor-crisp slim-oval heads, bowed-right quill stems, paired tapered-wedge beams, and wide double-bar binary divisions.
hero_scarlatti_madrid_sonata.paleography_notes: Models the sumptuous royal oblong harpsichord sonata codices copied at the Madrid/Aranjuez court for Queen Maria Barbara (Venice Marciana & Parma Palatina manuscripts, c. 1749-1757): sharply pared Iberian/Italian goose quill (42 deg, 0.17 min-ratio) cutting sleek slim-oval noteheads (scale 0.84, aspect 0.52) with brisk 12.5-deg forward poise, bowed-right stems, calligraphic-ribbon flags, tapered-wedge keyboard beams grouped in dazzling binary pairs (pair_beams_2) with steep arpeggio contours, tall spindly G-clefs, generously spaced court key signatures, wide-gap double barlines marking Scarlatti's signature binary repeats, and disciplined 28-stroke espresso-umber iron-gall cadence on luminous cream laid paper.

hero_rameau_paris_opera_score.name: hero_rameau_paris_opera_score
hero_rameau_paris_opera_score.description: Jean-Philippe Rameau's Paris Opera tragedie en musique full score (c. 1737): bold chevron-wedge heads, French broken secondary beams, tall overshooting barlines, and dark Parisian oak-gall ink.

hero_copland_brooklyn_pencil.name: hero_copland_brooklyn_pencil

hero_copland_brooklyn_pencil.paleography_notes: Models Aaron Copland's poised, Boulanger-disciplined graphite manuscripts (Appalachian Spring / Billy the Kid era, c. 1938-1945): sharpened medium #2B architectural pencil (0.78 min-ratio, 0.44 paper-tooth grain, zero ink dip) on crisp bright-white American score paper, upright compact noteheads (2.0-degree slant), straight classic stems, sharp angular 7-flags, horizontal flat wide-spaced beams, crisp angular modern clefs, wide-spread key signatures, Stravinsky-style geometric Z rests, generous blank pre-ruled staves (0.52), and frequent clean sculpting erasures (0.58).

hero_bernstein_dakota_conductor.name: hero_bernstein_dakota_conductor
hero_bernstein_dakota_conductor.description: Theatrical Dakota conductor's score (Leonard Bernstein, c. 1957-1971): bold crimson-red grease pencil on cool Ozalid blue transparency stock, oversized heavy-wedge heads, sweeping long-phrase beams, and emphatic podium cues.
hero_bernstein_dakota_conductor.paleography_notes: Captures Leonard Bernstein's kinetic, larger-than-life podium and composing scores at The Dakota (West Side Story / NY Philharmonic era, c. 1957-1975): heavily pressed crimson-red conductor's wax/graphite pencil (0.48 dry-wax grain, 1.44 stroke scale, zero ink dip) over cool Ozalid blue-tinted orchestral transparency paper, oversized heavy-wedge noteheads (scale 1.28) legible at arm's length, thick stems and marker-weight long-phrase beams with exaggerated theatrical swoop, bold figure-8 treble clefs, oversized accidentals, tall overshooting barlines, and dense podium marginalia (0.86).

hero_sondheim_broadway_legal_pad.name: hero_sondheim_broadway_legal_pad
hero_sondheim_broadway_legal_pad.description: Turtle Bay Broadway composer's legal-pad draft (Stephen Sondheim, c. 1979): velvety Blackwing 602 graphite on warm canary-yellow pad paper, syllabic all-flags-vocal notation, constant eraser ghosts, and dense lyric marginalia.
hero_sondheim_broadway_legal_pad.paleography_notes: Models Stephen Sondheim's legendary Turtle Bay couch-composing manuscripts (Company / Sweeney Todd / Sunday in the Park with George, c. 1970-2005): velvety soft Blackwing 602 dark graphite (0.40 tooth grain, zero ink dip) on unmistakable warm canary-yellow legal-pad spiral stock, compact neat oval noteheads, subtly bowed-left stems, syllabic vocal-score un-beamed flagging (all_flags_vocal with hooked J-tail flags), stubby compact clefs, tiny precise accidentals, tight double-gap barlines, heavy perfectionist eraser smudges (0.82), and dense lyric/rhyme margin notes (0.78).

hero_ellington_strayhorn_score.name: hero_ellington_strayhorn_score
hero_ellington_strayhorn_score.description: Sweeping 1940s Duke Ellington & Billy Strayhorn big-band arranger short score in warm sepia-ebony fountain ink with 16-deg swing slant, slashing heads, and paired swooping beams.
hero_ellington_strayhorn_score.paleography_notes: Modeled on Duke Ellington and Billy Strayhorn touring-train and hotel-room big-band short scores in the Smithsonian Ellington Archives (c. 1940-1946, Take the A Train / Black, Brown and Beige era). Written rapidly with a supple medium-broad fountain pen in warm sepia-ebony ink on buff 12-staff band paper: exuberant 16.0 deg forward swing slant, angled slash noteheads, flexible S-curve stems, wide horizontal-wing flags, overhanging swooping beams grouped in swung eighth-note pairs (pair_beams_2), figure-8 treble clefs, wide slanted accidentals, tall overshooting barlines, studio-copyist reverse-3 rests, abundant blank section staves, and dense soloist/mute marginalia.

hero_coltrane_giant_steps_ink.name: hero_coltrane_giant_steps_ink
hero_coltrane_giant_steps_ink.description: Hyper-dense 1959-1964 John Coltrane sheets-of-sound harmonic notebook in saturated navy-black fountain ink with compact noteheads, crammed steep phrase beams, and packed bar endings.
hero_coltrane_giant_steps_ink.paleography_notes: Inspired by John Coltrane harmonic cycle notebooks and studio charts (1959-1964, Giant Steps / Countdown / A Love Supreme era). Written intently in saturated navy-black fountain-pen ink on buff aged manuscript pads: small compact noteheads packed tightly across nearly every staff (minimal blank staves, severe end-of-bar cramming), steep forward-slanted stems, angular 7-flags, tight-crammed long-phrase beams racing along steep melodic contours, tall spindly G-clefs, densely clustered accidentals for rapid third-relation modulations, tight double barlines, and brisk bebop napkin-tick rests.

hero_miles_davis_modal_sketch.name: hero_miles_davis_modal_sketch
hero_miles_davis_modal_sketch.description: Spare, cool 1959 Miles Davis Kind of Blue studio modal sketch in dry slate-graphite pencil with minimalist vertical-tick noteheads, detached stems, and vast open blank staves.
hero_miles_davis_modal_sketch.paleography_notes: Evokes Miles Davis sparse modal scale and head sketches brought to Columbia 30th Street Studio for the 1959 Kind of Blue sessions (So What, Flamenco Sketches, Blue in Green). Jotted with a dry slate-graphite wooden pencil on crisp white studio lead-sheet stock: radically minimal vertical-tick noteheads with open hollow loops, detached-gap stems, minimal dot-tail flags, broken gapped high-floating beams with mixed split flags, bare-bones S-slash clefs, wide-spread accidentals, short clipped barlines, pinprick V-tick rests, extensive eraser rub-outs, and vast open blank staves leaving room for improvisation.

hero_mingus_workshop_ink.name: hero_mingus_workshop_ink
hero_mingus_workshop_ink.description: Volcanic 1956-1963 Charles Mingus Jazz Workshop score in heavy wet carbon-black ink with massive wedge noteheads, double-pass scribbled beams, wild clefs, and turbulent stains.
hero_mingus_workshop_ink.paleography_notes: Modeled on Charles Mingus tempestuous Jazz Workshop working scores and Epitaph / Black Saint and the Sinner Lady manuscripts (1956-1963). Slashed onto worn aged-rag score paper with a heavy wet broad-nib pen in dense carbon-black ink: oversized heavy-wedge noteheads, stems overshooting noteheads, stubby wedge flags, thick double-pass scribbled beams arched in uneven 3+1 stop-time groupings, wild Beethoven-like slash clefs, oversized bold accidentals, double-pass overshooting barlines, violent zigzag rests, heavy ink pooling and feathering, warping staves, and intense rehearsal marginalia.

hero_gil_evans_orchestral_pencil.name: hero_gil_evans_orchestral_pencil
hero_gil_evans_orchestral_pencil.description: Luminous 1957-1960 Gil Evans orchestral-jazz master score in fine 2H/HB draftsman graphite on translucent cyan Ozalid vellum with slim-diamond heads, needle stems, and vast open tacet staves.
hero_gil_evans_orchestral_pencil.paleography_notes: Modeled on Gil Evans luminous orchestral-jazz master scores (1957-1960, Miles Ahead / Porgy and Bess / Sketches of Spain). Drafted with a sharply pointed 2H/HB draftsman graphite pencil on pale cyan-blue translucent Ozalid vellum: ultra-refined slim-diamond noteheads, tall hairline-needle stems, feathered-sweep flags, wide-spaced gentle beams with French broken secondary grouping reflecting Evans Impressionist orchestration, classic engraved clefs, hairline-needle accidentals, faint hairline barlines, needle-S rests, crisp block bar rests, soft voicing-revision eraser clouds, and generous blank orchestral tacet staves.

hero_korngold_warner_ozalid.name: hero_korngold_warner_ozalid
hero_korngold_warner_ozalid.description: 1938 Golden-Age Warner Bros. diazo Ozalid blueprint part (Korngold era): vivid cobalt-blue ink on cool cyan stock, Viennese teardrop heads, and sweeping calligraphic phrase beams.
hero_korngold_warner_ozalid.paleography_notes: Modeled on 1935-1946 Warner Bros. Burbank music-department scores and parts for Erich Wolfgang Korngold (The Adventures of Robin Hood, The Sea Hawk, Kings Row), penned on translucent vellum and duplicated via ammonia diazo Ozalid into unmistakable cobalt-indigo lines on pale cyan stock. Fuses opulent Viennese calligraphy (41 deg nib, 0.22 min-ratio, plush teardrop noteheads, flared-base stems, calligraphic-ribbon flags and convex-arch long-phrase beams) with disciplined Hollywood sight-reading layout, classic engraved clefs, wide-spread key signatures, serifed barlines, and studio-copyist clean-3 rests.

hero_herrmann_hitchcock_ink.name: hero_herrmann_hitchcock_ink
hero_herrmann_hitchcock_ink.description: 1960 Bernard Herrmann self-orchestrated Hitchcock full score in brooding wet carbon-black fountain ink: heavy-wedge noteheads, slashing steep ostinato beams, and tall overshooting barlines.
hero_herrmann_hitchcock_ink.paleography_notes: Modeled on Bernard Herrmann's fierce, self-orchestrated full orchestral autographs for Alfred Hitchcock (Vertigo 1958, North by Northwest 1959, Psycho 1960), written directly in dense black fountain-pen ink on heavy buff studio manuscript paper without orchestrators. Defined by thunderous wet nib pressure (stroke_scale 1.46, ink_pooling 0.44, ink_dip_period 24), stabbing heavy-wedge noteheads (scale 1.22, -38 deg), stems that overshoot the notehead, sharp angular-7 flags, heavy marker beams driven along steep contours in tense uneven 3+1 ostinato groupings, wild slashed clefs, oversized bold accidentals, dramatic tall-overshoot barlines, bold chevron rests, and dense bowing/dynamic marginalia.

hero_hisaishi_tokyo_studio_pencil.name: hero_hisaishi_tokyo_studio_pencil
hero_hisaishi_tokyo_studio_pencil.description: Tokyo Studio Ghibli orchestral scoring-stage pencil manuscript (Joe Hisaishi era, 1984-2013): crisp 0.5mm B mechanical graphite on pristine bright-white stock with lyrical slim-oval heads and tidy erasures.
hero_hisaishi_tokyo_studio_pencil.paleography_notes: Evokes Joe Hisaishi's Tokyo orchestral and piano scoring manuscripts for Studio Ghibli (Nausicaa, Totoro, Princess Mononoke, Spirited Away, 1984-2013) drafted with a crisp 0.5mm B/2B mechanical drafting pencil on smooth bright-white Japanese B4 studio score paper. Balances architectural Japanese precision (near-uniform nib_min_ratio 0.88, low 0.44 px wobble, crisp vertical barlines, classic neat key signatures, straight engraver-gentle standard-beat beams) with warm graphite tooth (grain_strength 0.30), lyrical slim-oval noteheads, slender tall-spindly G-clefs, delicate gossamer-3 quarter rests, hollow-box sketch bar rests, and clean eraser rub-outs from cue-timing revisions.

hero_sakamoto_tokyo_fineliner.name: hero_sakamoto_tokyo_fineliner
hero_sakamoto_tokyo_fineliner.description: Ryuichi Sakamoto austere 0.3mm archival black pigment-liner score (1983-2017): razor-thin hairline-dash heads, tall needle stems, high-floating French broken beams, and Zen white space.
hero_sakamoto_tokyo_fineliner.paleography_notes: Inspired by Ryuichi Sakamoto's spare, post-Debussy piano and cinema manuscripts (Merry Christmas Mr. Lawrence, The Last Emperor, Playing the Piano, async, 1983-2017) inked with a razor-fine 0.3mm Japanese archival pigment fineliner on stark white architectural manuscript paper. Immediately recognizable by its monolinear gossamer stroke (stroke_scale 0.56, nib_min_ratio 0.96, zero pooling), minimalist hairline-dash noteheads (aspect 0.48), tall hairline-needle stems (1.24x), minimal dot-tail flags, hairline-thin high-floating beams with Debussy-inspired French broken secondary grouping, stripped minimal S-slash clefs, needle accidentals, faint barlines, pinprick-V quarter rests, and expansive blank-stave negative space.

hero_uematsu_jrpg_notebook.name: hero_uematsu_jrpg_notebook
hero_uematsu_jrpg_notebook.description: 1990s Tokyo JRPG melody & battle-theme spiral notebook (Nobuo Uematsu era): dark pine-teal sign pen, punchy compact arpeggio heads, tight stepped pair-beams, and late-night bar cramming.
hero_uematsu_jrpg_notebook.paleography_notes: Evokes Nobuo Uematsu's exuberant 1987-2001 Tokyo game-studio composition notebooks (Final Fantasy IV, VI, VII, VIII) jotted late at night in a wire-bound spiral manuscript pad with a Japanese 0.5mm fiber-tip sign pen in distinctive dark pine-teal ink. Built for rapid prog-rock-meets-Baroque arpeggios and looping battle ostinatos: punchy compact noteheads (scale 0.88), brisk bowed-right stems (0.90x), tiny-flick flags, tight-crammed beams with stepped secondary tilt in energetic pair-beams-2 groupings, stubby compact clefs, tightly clustered key signatures, clipped inside barlines, quick napkin-tick quarter rests, wavy ledgers, heavy end-of-bar cramming, coffee-ring stains, and abundant loop/synth-patch marginalia.

hero_flamenco_jerez_guitar_sketch.name: hero_flamenco_jerez_guitar_sketch
hero_flamenco_jerez_guitar_sketch.description: Andalusian Jerez de la Frontera flamenco guitar falseta sketch (c. 1968): fiery garnet-sepia ink, aggressive rasgueado slash heads, frantic zigzag flags, uneven 3+1 compas beaming, and wine-stained cream stock.
hero_flamenco_jerez_guitar_sketch.paleography_notes: Evokes working Andalusian flamenco guitarist falseta and compas notebooks from Jerez de la Frontera (c. 1960s-1970s): warm garnet-sepia felt/fountain ink over sun-baked cream manuscript stock, aggressive diagonal slash noteheads (-44 deg, 14.5 deg forward velocity) capturing rasgueado and picado impulse, overshooting stems, frantic zigzag flags, double-pass scribbled beams grouped in asymmetric 3+1 compas clusters with steep contour slopes, minimal S-slash clefs, wide slanted Phrygian sharps, slashed repeat-tick barlines, hurried napkin-tick rests, and dense margin beat-count annotations.

hero_klezmer_odessa_fiddle_book.name: hero_klezmer_odessa_fiddle_book
hero_klezmer_odessa_fiddle_book.description: Turn-of-the-century Odessa klezmer fiddler tune book (c. 1905): oxidized soot-plum dip ink, pooled ink-blot heads, S-curved stems, double-loop ornament flags, oversized repeat dots, and foxed travel-worn rag.
hero_klezmer_odessa_fiddle_book.paleography_notes: Modeled on turn-of-the-20th-century Eastern European klezmer violin tune books from Odessa and the Beregovski archive (c. 1895-1915): steel dip-pen in oxidized soot-plum ink with 19-stroke dip-cycle shading, heavy ink feathering (0.42), split-nib tracks (0.28), and reverse-side bleed-through on foxed hand-rastrumed rag. Features pooled ink-blot noteheads, expressive S-curve flex stems, ornate double-back-loop flags, sagged concave phrase-long beams with reverse-quirk slopes, provincial figure-8 treble clefs, jagged zigzag freygish accidentals, oversized repeat-blob barlines for bulgar/freylekhs dances, and Russian-school looped-2 quarter rests.

hero_irish_clare_session_pad.name: hero_irish_clare_session_pad
hero_irish_clare_session_pad.description: County Clare Irish trad session pocket spiral pad (c. 1982): soft 2B graphite pencil, compact reel noteheads, tight-hug crammed beams, eraser smudges, and stout-ringed pad paper.
hero_irish_clare_session_pad.paleography_notes: Captures a working County Clare (Doolin/Ennis) traditional Irish session musician pocket spiral pad (c. 1975-1995): soft 2B graphite pencil (high grain 0.44, zero ink pooling, heavy eraser smudging 0.54) jotting 32-bar AABB reels and jigs on a knee between tunes. Compact small noteheads (scale 0.82) with severe end-of-bar cramming (0.42), bowed-left stems, tiny-flick grace-note flags, tight-crammed beams hugging the noteheads in standard beat groups, stubby compact treble clefs, crammed D/G-major sharp clusters, tight double-gap A/B barlines, and pinprick V rests on pub-stained spiral paper.

hero_choro_rio_notebook_pen.name: hero_choro_rio_notebook_pen
hero_choro_rio_notebook_pen.description: Rio de Janeiro roda de choro caderno (c. 1962): royal-cobalt Bic Cristal ballpoint on vintage mint-tinted Brazilian music ledger paper, nimble hairline-dash heads, hooked J-flags, and broken 16th-note syncopation beams.
hero_choro_rio_notebook_pen.paleography_notes: Inspired by Rio de Janeiro roda de choro bandolim and flute notebooks (Pixinguinha / Jacob do Bandolim era, c. 1955-1972): fine royal-cobalt Bic Cristal ballpoint (uniform nib_min_ratio 0.92, zero dip cycle, light ballpoint dropout 0.12) on pale mint-green tinted Brazilian caderno de musica stock. Swift hairline-dash noteheads (scale 0.86, aspect 0.58) capture rapid 16th-note baixaria and melody runs, paired with forward-bowed stems, lilting hooked-J flags, stepped-wobbly beams in French broken-secondary grouping for syncopated subdivisions, hurried single-loop clefs, ascending-drift key signatures, gapped ballpoint barlines, and floating-tilde rests.

hero_abbey_road_string_session.name: hero_abbey_road_string_session
hero_abbey_road_string_session.description: 1967 London EMI Abbey Road Studio Two pop-orchestral string session part: razor-crisp jet-black copyist chisel ink on bright white stock, heavy-wedge heads, flat wide-spaced beams, and bold sight-reading accidentals.
hero_abbey_road_string_session.paleography_notes: Models 1966-1969 London EMI Abbey Road Studio Two orchestral pop/rock session parts (George Martin / British Union studio copyist house hand): authoritative jet-black ink from a broad chisel-cut music fountain pen (38 deg, 0.28 min-ratio, smooth 42-stroke reservoir cadence) on bright white pre-printed studio stock. Engineered for instant Take-1 sight-reading: commanding heavy-wedge noteheads (scale 1.16, aspect 1.14), upright straight stems, wide horizontal-wing flags, flat wide-spaced beams (1.34x thickness) on strict beat boundaries, classic engraved clefs, oversized bold chromatic accidentals, wide double-gap rehearsal barlines, and clean studio-copyist reverse-3 rests.
